## Subscriber appeals

The service implements all three homework 4 tasks. `POST /appeals` validates
subscriber details, one or more problem reasons, and the detection time with
Pydantic, then saves each accepted appeal as a separate JSON file.
See the [Subscriber appeals API guide](docs/appeals.md) for a runnable example,
validation rules, storage configuration, and tests. No database is required.

## Development

This project contains one FastAPI service, `app`, in `services/app/`.
Follow the [Developer quickstart](docs/quickstart.md) for setup, local
infrastructure, a working FastAPI example, and the daily development workflow.

```bash
uv tool install rust-just
just bootstrap
uv run pre-commit install
just check
uv run --package app uvicorn app.main:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000 --reload
```

Open <http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs> for the API documentation. Health endpoints are
`/health/live` and `/health/ready`.

Members contain an editable `pyproject.toml`, `src/<package>/`, and `tests/`.
Services also have a FastAPI `app`, a Dockerfile that starts Uvicorn on port 80,
and `k8s/` defaults for a Deployment, a ClusterIP Service, and Kustomize. Each service
README explains image configuration and deployment. Libraries contain Python
packages without deployment files. Root `tests/` contains integration tests.

Service `main.py` assembles the application and its lifespan; `routers/health.py`
provides `/health/live` and `/health/ready` for HTTP probes. Readiness returns 503
when the instance is unavailable. Add route groups under `routers/` and register
them in `create_app()`.

Use `just new-service <name>` or `just new-lib <name>`, optionally followed by a
description: `just new-lib common "Shared utilities"`.
Names must be unique lowercase Python identifiers. Run `just` to list commands.
Kubernetes names default to package names with underscores replaced by hyphens;
they must fit in 63 characters and end in a letter or digit. Customize
`kubernetes_name` in `templates/service/cookiecutter.json` when needed.
Customize scaffolds in `templates/service/` and `templates/lib/` independently.
Creation refreshes this README through `templates/readme/README.md.jinja`, which
includes `header.md.jinja` for the tables. Run `just codegen` after manually
adding, removing, or renaming members. `just check-generated` checks for drift.
Member READMEs contain direct Markdown links and remain yours to edit.

`just bootstrap` installs shared dev/docs tools and creates `.env` from
`.env.example` if missing. `just test`, `just lint`, and `just check` run each
member independently, then the integration scope. Append a scope to select it,
such as `just test services/app` or `just check integration`. Each test scope has
its own environment under `.venvs/` and output under `reports/`. Checks continue across
members and return failure if any member fails. An empty integration suite is
allowed; a member without tests fails its test check.

Each member's pytest configuration uses `testpaths = ["tests"]` and coverage of
its own `src/`. Root pytest configuration covers integration tests only. These
files stay editable; creating a member does not regenerate them.

Manage runtime versions in the root `pyproject.toml`, where Dependabot maintains
them. Run `uv add <dependency>` from the repository root, then list the dependency
name and required extras without a version bound in each member that uses it.
Members retain these declarations so isolated tests and container builds install
their runtime requirements. The shared `uv.lock` resolves versions across the
whole workspace. Shared tooling uses root dependency groups, and the integration
environment installs all members. Commit manifest changes and `uv.lock` together.
`just format`, `just docs`, `just serve`, and `just reports` are also available.
See [Development tools](docs/tools.md) for the testing tools, their purposes,
and setup requirements.
See [infra/README.md](infra/README.md) to start PostgreSQL, Redis, Prometheus,
and Grafana, configure database connections, and add application metrics targets.

## Browser tests

pytest-playwright is included in the shared `dev` group. Before running UI tests,
install a browser with `uv run --group dev python -m playwright install chromium`
and start the application under test. Linux CI also needs browser OS dependencies
(`playwright install --with-deps chromium`). Run tests in the selected scope
with `just test integration`, `just test services/<name>`, or `just test libs/<name>`.
Browser failure videos are retained automatically under `reports/<scope>/playwright/`
and attached to the failed Allure test by the shared root `conftest.py`.
Passing recordings are discarded. See [the report guide](docs/ci-reports.md#browser-failure-videos)
for configuration and overrides.

## GitHub setup and reports

Pants infers dependencies from Python imports using each member's `BUILD` file.
PR CI selects changed members and their transitive dependents, plus integration.
Shared changes, deletions, and default-branch runs check every member. uv and Just
continue to install packages and run checks. Declare relationships that cannot be
inferred from imports explicitly in `BUILD`; no graph regeneration is needed.
With the [Pants launcher](https://www.pantsbuild.org/stable/docs/getting-started/installing-pants)
installed, use `pants dependencies --transitive services/app:member` to inspect
relationships.

Pull requests retain report artifacts. The default branch publishes documentation,
member coverage, Allure reports/history, and Shields endpoints to GitHub Pages.
Each member's badges use only that member's check results. Integration coverage
is reported separately.

GitHub Pages is configured to publish through GitHub Actions at
<https://alexxios.github.io/python-course-project/>. README badges and member
templates already point to this site's reports. The first successful default-branch
workflow publishes them; future members inherit these links from their templates.

Dependabot updates Python dependencies, Actions, pre-commit hooks, Allure, and
service and infrastructure container images weekly. See [the report guide](docs/ci-reports.md) for
Pages layout, setup, and history details.
